title: Primitive recursion inside Peano arithmetic

based_on.title: Provability logic: models within models in Peano Arithmetic
An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: A finite recursive recipe gives one arithmetic proof of totality, uniqueness and its defining equations.
abstract: Knowing a separate proof for each numerical calculation does not give one proof that every calculation has an answer. Peano arithmetic can prove that stronger assertion for functions built by primitive recursion. We construct their graphs from their finite recipes, record a recursion as a coded history, and prove its totality and uniqueness by two explicit induction arguments. The graph can be normalized to an existential formula with only bounded tests, while retaining PA proofs of the same equations. A worked doubling example and a comparison criterion explain what is needed to use those equations at nonstandard inputs.
